kangaroo-at-2020-student-01.prompt: What is the last digit of the result of the multiplication $1\times3\times5\times7\times9^2\times7\times5\times3\times1$?

kangaroo-at-2020-student-02.prompt: An ant walked 6 m every day to go from point A to point B in a straight line. One day Johnny put a straight cylinder one metre high in the way. Now the ant walks on the same straight line or above it, having to go up and down the cylinder, as shown in the picture. How far does she have to walk now to go from A to B?

kangaroo-at-2020-student-03.prompt: How many integers are there between $2020.9^2$ and $2018.9\times2022.9$?

kangaroo-at-2020-student-05.prompt: The pie chart shows the number of inhabitants of the five zones of a city. The central zone has the same population as the north, west and east zones together and the south zone has half of the inhabitants of the west zone. What is the percentage difference between the inhabitants of the north and east zones?

kangaroo-at-2020-student-06.prompt: Let $a$, $b$ and $c$ be integers such that $1\le a\le b\le c$ and $abc=2020^2$. What is the highest possible value of $a$?

kangaroo-at-2020-student-07.prompt: Which of the following numbers is divisible by 3, whatever the integer $n$?

kangaroo-at-2020-student-08.prompt: If a dozen nanica bananas cost the same as ten prata bananas and $y$ nanica bananas cost $x$ reais, how many reais do $z$ prata bananas cost?
kangaroo-at-2020-student-08.reviewNote: The English source says "a dozen nanica bananas cost the same as a dozen prata bananas", which would give $xz/y$ (not an option). The official answer (C) matches "a dozen nanicas cost the same as ten pratas"; the prompt was corrected accordingly — please check against the original Portuguese.

kangaroo-at-2020-student-09.prompt: Two equal dice have two red faces, two blue and two green each. If we roll the two dice simultaneously, what is the probability that the result will be two faces with different colours?

kangaroo-at-2020-student-10.prompt:
In the addition below, different letters represent different digits (a leading digit may be 0). Assuming the sum is correct, what is the highest possible value for the sum C + A + N?

$$\begin{array}{r} C\,A\,N \\ +\;G\,U\,R \\ \hline U\,U\,U \end{array}$$
kangaroo-at-2020-student-10.reviewNote: The source prints the addition CAN + GUR = UUU as a picture. The official answer 21 needs G = 0 (498 + 057 = 555); if leading zeros were forbidden the maximum would be 20, so the prompt states that a leading digit may be 0.

kangaroo-at-2020-student-11.prompt: A grey square with an area of 36 cm² and a black square with an area of 25 cm² are superimposed, as shown. What is the perimeter of the overlapping region, represented by the white quadrilateral, which has a vertex on a side of the grey square?
kangaroo-at-2020-student-11.reviewNote: The official key lists (B) 11 cm, which is impossible (two sides alone are 5 cm + 4 cm, and the computed perimeter is 18 cm). The keys of questions 10 and 11 may be swapped; answer set to (D) by computation.

kangaroo-at-2020-student-12.prompt: Two thousand and twenty coins are on a table, with "heads" facing up. With each move you must turn over exactly three of these coins. What is the smallest number of moves you must make so that all the coins on the table have "tails" facing up?

choices.text: It is not possible to make all the coins show "tails".

kangaroo-at-2020-student-13.prompt: Zilda will use six equal cubes and two different rectangular blocks to form the structure shown, which has eight faces. Before gluing the pieces, she will paint each one entirely, and she calculated that she would need 18 litres of paint (the colour does not matter). How many litres of paint would she use if she painted the whole structure only after gluing the parts?

kangaroo-at-2020-student-14.prompt: Let $a$, $b$ and $c$ be non-zero real numbers such that $(a-a^{-1})^2+(b-b^{-1})^2+(c-c^{-1})^2=0$. Which number below can NOT be the value of $a+b+c$?

kangaroo-at-2020-student-15.prompt: The last two digits of a 2020-digit number are 9 and 9. At most, how many digits does the square of that number have?

kangaroo-at-2020-student-16.prompt: The sequence $f_n$ is given by $f_1=1$, $f_2=2$ and $f_n=f_{n-1}\cdot f_{n+1}$ for $n\ge2$. How many of the first 2020 terms of this sequence are even numbers?

kangaroo-at-2020-student-17.prompt: Matias wrote 15 numbers on the wheel shown. Only one of them is visible, the 10 on top of the wheel. The sum of the numbers in any seven consecutive positions, such as the grey positions in the figure, is always the same. When seven numbers in consecutive positions are added up, which of the following results is possible?

kangaroo-at-2020-student-18.prompt: A large square touches another two squares, as shown in the picture. The numbers inside the smaller squares indicate their areas. What is the area of the largest square?

kangaroo-at-2020-student-19.prompt: A circle is tangent to one side of a rectangle and passes through two of its vertices, as shown. A square of area 20 cm² has one side on the side of the rectangle and two vertices on the circle, as shown in the figure. What is the area of the rectangle?

kangaroo-at-2020-student-20.prompt: Two rectangular blocks and a cube are joined to form a larger rectangular block, whose volume is 280 cm³. The cube, in dark grey in the picture, has volume 125 cm³ and the smaller rectangular block has volume 75 cm³. What is the area of the face marked with the question mark?

kangaroo-at-2020-student-21.prompt: The figure shows the lines $r$ and $s$, whose equations are $y=ax+b$ and $y=cx+d$ respectively. Which of the following statements is true?

kangaroo-at-2020-student-22.prompt: A little kangaroo draws a line passing through point P of the grid and then paints three triangles in black as shown in the picture. The areas of these triangles are proportional to which numbers?

kangaroo-at-2020-student-23.prompt: A rectangular garden was 50 m long and 40 m wide. An artificial lake was built next to it, so that the whole forms a 60 m square. Then a fence was stretched, separating both the garden and the lake into two parts with equal areas, as shown in the picture. How long is this fence?

kangaroo-at-2020-student-24.prompt: A positive integer $N$ is divisible by all integers from 2 to 11 except two of these numbers. Among the pairs of integers (6,7), (7,8), (8,9), (9,10) and (10,11), how many could be the exception?

kangaroo-at-2020-student-25.prompt: At the Sunday fair, in the morning Ana wanted to buy three types of fruit among 12 options and one type of vegetable among the six types available. In the afternoon some products were sold out and Bela wanted to buy two kinds of fruit and two kinds of vegetables among the remaining ones. Since the number of possible choices for Bela was a quarter of the number of possible choices for Ana, how many products were sold out in the afternoon?

kangaroo-at-2020-student-26.prompt: Vilma took a sheet of paper measuring 10 cm × 20 cm and made two folds, taking the two shorter sides of the sheet onto a diagonal. She gets a parallelogram, as shown in the picture. What is the area of this quadrilateral, in cm²?

kangaroo-at-2020-student-27.prompt: The submerged volume of an iceberg in the form of a cube corresponds to 96.4% of the volume of the iceberg. The part outside the water has three equal edges (it is a corner of the cube). What percentage of the total surface area of the iceberg is in contact with the air?

kangaroo-at-2020-student-28.prompt: Maria writes all the positive divisors of 2020, one on each card, and puts all these cards in a box. Then she closes her eyes and starts taking these cards out of the box, one by one. How many cards must she take out of the box to make sure that among the cards taken there are two with numbers $a$ and $b$ such that $a$ is not a divisor of $b$ and $b$ is not a divisor of $a$?

kangaroo-at-2020-student-29.prompt: There are $n$ different prime numbers $p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_n$ written from left to right in the bottom row of the table shown. The product of two neighbouring numbers in the same row is written in the box above them. The number $K=p_1^{\alpha_1}p_2^{\alpha_2}\cdots p_n^{\alpha_n}$ is written in the top box. In a table like this, in which $\alpha_2=9$, how many numbers are divisible by $p_4$?

kangaroo-at-2020-student-30.prompt: Adam and Bruna try to find out which is Carla's favourite figure among the figures shown. Adam knows that Carla told Bruna the shape of the figure. Bruna knows that Carla told Adam the colour of the figure. The following conversation takes place. Adam: "I don't know what Carla's favourite figure is and I know that Bruna doesn't know either." Bruna: "At first I didn't know what Carla's favourite figure was, but now I know." Adam: "Now I know too." What is Carla's favourite figure?
